exposure: planned vaginal birth after previous cesarean (VBAC)
cohort: 47,414 women in Scotland with 1 or more previous cesarean sections giving birth to a singleton at term between 1983 and 1996
finding: Planned VBAC, compared to ERCS, was associated with a greater than 2-fold increased risk of undergoing pelvic floor surgery.
mod_finding: Women who had a planned VBAC had a 2- to 3-fold increased risk of having surgery for pelvic organ prolapse or urinary incontinence compared to women who had a planned ERCS.
